gnomes:
Round all our homes,
Kobolds and gnomes do daily cling,
Then nightly fling their lanterns out.
gnome:
Or dome of worm,
Or porch of gnome,
Or some elf's catacomb?

If ruff it was of dame
Or shroud of gnome,
Himself, himself inform.
gnomon: It had always sounded strangely in my ears, like the word gnomon in the Euclid and the word simony in the Catechism.
gnostic: John himself, or whatever early Gnostic took his name and mantle--I see the continual assertion of the imagination as the basis of all spiritual and material life, I see also that to Christ imagination was simply a form of love, and that to him love was lord in the fullest meaning of the phrase.
gnomic: They often say in their Gnomic aphorisms, 'Even the Gods cannot alter the past.
